title: All Nature Feels Attractive Power
description: All Nature Feels Attractive Power in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: William Drennan wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 381 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Law of Love”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: All na-ture feels at-trac-tive power, A strong, em-brac-ing force; The drops that spark-le in the shower, The plan-ets in their course.

lines: All nature feels attractive power,
A strong, embracing force;
The drops that sparkle in the shower,
The planets in their course.
Thus, in the universe of mind,
Is felt the law of love;
The charity both strong and kind,
For all that live and move.
In this fine sympathetic chain
All creatures bear a part;
Their every pleasure, every pain,
Linked to the feeling heart.
More perfect bond, the Christian plan
Attaches soul to soul;
Our neighbor is the suffering man,
Though at the farthest pole.
To earth below, from heaven above,
The faith in Christ professed,
More clearly shows that God is love,
And whom he loves is blessed.

licence: Public domain: William Drennan died in 1820.
credits: Words by William Drennan (1754–1820), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
